notes: The page begins with heading 6, not inside a speech, so opens_mid_utterance is false. Eighteen printed labels, eighteen turns: the chair speaks repeatedly in a row ('Lo ponemos en consideración.' then, after the votación note, 'Aprobado por unanimidad.', and in section 7 'Aprobado por unanimidad.' followed immediately by a separately labelled 'Por favor, senador Zamora.'), and each printed label is counted, per rule 2. Unlabelled indented paragraphs that follow a label are NOT counted as new turns: 'Si no se hace uso de la palabra, se va a votar.', 'Le vamos a tomar juramento al senador Pinedo.', the two oath formulas addressed to Pinedo and to Zamora ('Señor senador don … ¿juráis a la Patria…?'), and 'Vamos a pedirle ahora, señora senadora, la propuesta de los secretarios.' — all of these continue the chair's preceding turn. '(Aplausos.)' appears twice printed inside the chair's own paragraph after 'os lo demanden.', so per rule 4 it is part of that turn's words and is not listed as an event; I left it out of first_words. The two stenographer notes are identical in wording, italic, indented, opening with a dash. Nothing here is an inserted document: the oath formulas are spoken by the chair. Both '¡Sí, juro!' turns are one-line answers and are easy to lose. The heading terminator is a full stop in all three, and heading 8 prints the ordinal as '1º' (masculine ordinal sign). Label weight is inconsistent across the page — sometimes the full stop before the hyphen is bold ('Sr. Presidente.-' in the juramento lines), sometimes roman ('Sr. Presidente.-' elsewhere) — but the characters are the same and I recorded one form. Rozas's turn runs on past the foot of the page.
